title: Bridgebuilder anthropic voice calls the Anthropic HTTP API (401 on a stale .env key) instead of the claude-headless hop under hounfour.headless.mode: cli-only
description: Observed 2026-09-22 on PR #1266, BB iterations 1–2: '[multi-model:anthropic] Review failed: cheval-delegate: INVALID_INPUT: [cheval] INVALID_INPUT: Anthropic API error (HTTP 401): API key is invalid.' post-merge pipeline is tag-only: release/stamp commits never fast-forward main, so main's CLAUDE.loa.md/.loa-version.json/CHANGELOG stay behind the tags
description: Discovered during cycle-118 deploy verification (v1.192.0). The header-stamp fix (bd-claude-loa-header-self-stamp, shipped #1188) WORKS: the version_bump phase ran ('Synced framework markers to v1.192.0 (committed: true)') and the v1.192.0 TAG tree correctly carries header 1.192.0 (first reliably-stamped tag; pre-fix tags were stale). BUT post-merge.yml pushes only the TAG (git push origin $TAG at :179) — it never fast-forwards/pushes the main BRANCH. So the release commits (a757a56c sync-markers, 6933d2f0 changelog) live only on the tag; origin/main HEAD stays at the PR-merge commit with header still 1.180.0. PRE-EXISTING + likely intentional (avoids a release bot force-pushing a protected main). CONSEQUENCE: consumers pinning the loa submodule at a TAG get the correct header (the bead's 'frozen across ~10 tags' goal is met); consumers tracking main HEAD see stale markers, and main's CHANGELOG/version never advance on-branch. DECISION for operator: (a) make the pipeline fast-forward/push main after tagging (needs branch-protection allowance for the release bot — sensitive), (b) accept tag-only releases as canonical + document that main markers are intentionally not release-advanced + ensure consumers pin tags not main, or (c) status quo. Not fixing ad-hoc — branch-protection-sensitive.

title: OPERATOR-ONLY: move audit root key cycle098-root.priv offline (agent MUST NOT run)
description:
OPERATOR-ONLY security action. AGENT MUST NOT RUN move-root-key-offline.sh -- it irreversibly shreds the root private key; a wrong/unmounted destination risks catastrophic, unrecoverable key loss. Admin pre-approval for the keepers does NOT extend to auto-running this.

Threat (verified): ~/.config/loa/audit-keys/cycle098-root.priv is an UNENCRYPTED Ed25519 root key on disk; its derived pubkey matches the pinned root-of-trust (.claude/data/maintainer-root-pubkey.txt). Anyone with this file can mint a forged trust-store (add an attacker writer key, drop revocations, re-sign with the root), and every forged audit envelope would then verify as authentic -- defeating the entire MODELINV/audit moat. The writer key (deep-name.priv) is separate and stays put; cheval keeps signing with it after the move.

Runbook (operator, by hand):
1. Mount an ENCRYPTED offline medium (LUKS/encrypted USB); note its mount path. The key is written in plaintext PEM, so the medium itself must be encrypted.
2. Confirm python3 + cryptography importable.
3. Run: ~/.config/loa/audit-keys/move-root-key-offline.sh <mounted-dest-dir>
   Expect [1/3 copied] -> [2/3 verified vs pinned pubkey] -> [3/3 source shredded]. The script is FAIL-CLOSED: on ENCRYPTED / MISMATCH / BADKEY it KEEPS the source and aborts -- STOP and investigate if you see those.
4. Verify after: source cycle098-root.priv gone; deep-name.priv still present; offline copy derives to pinned pubkey MCowBQYDK2VwAyEAdXgpsndtu9p+fI3Rw/rqr+LjQYtOrZKsXgHKN974o+M= ; audit chain + trust-store still verify green.
5. Unmount, store the medium offline.
Caveat: FS is ext4; shred on SSD is best-effort -> full-disk + medium encryption is the real protection.

This blocks NO code work (D1/D2/D3 proceed independently). Priority P1 (highest real security leverage in the set).
